concerns.text: FR-004 mandates identifying a tipping point where error exceeds nominal [deferred] level by >10% relative increase. The 'nominal [deferred]' placeholder makes the threshold unmeasurable. The spec must explicitly state the nominal alpha (e.g., 0.05) to allow verification of the 10% relative increase condition.

SC-001 states the target is '≤ 6%' but references 'nominal [deferred]'. The success criterion is unmeasurable because the baseline (nominal alpha) is deferred. The spec must define the nominal alpha (e.g., 0.05) to verify if 6% is the correct 20% relative inflation threshold.

SC-002 defines the tipping point condition as 'exceeds 5.5% ([deferred] relative increase)'. The parenthetical '[deferred] relative increase' contradicts the explicit 5.5% value (which implies a 10% increase over 5%). This ambiguity prevents a deterministic pass/fail check for the tipping point logic.

SC-005 requires measuring 'CC error > 2 * MI error'. While the multiplier is defined, the 'MI error' reference is ambiguous without a defined condition (e.g., 'at the identified tipping point' or 'across all rates'). The criterion needs a specific context to be verifiable.

User Story 2 Acceptance Scenario 2 uses '5.5% ([deferred] relative increase)'. The text mixes a concrete value with a deferred placeholder for the same concept, creating confusion. It should either state '5.5% (a 10% relative increase over 5%)' or defer the entire threshold.
